purpose: Enterprise readiness audit, gap register, and next-step program for stabilizing the full MarketingOps web platform.

readiness_summary.headline: The platform now has a credible enterprise backbone, but it still needs consolidation, release discipline, and security completion to become fully enterprise-grade.
strongest_areas: Canonical truth and collection around Data Collection, the master database, and the property registry
Governed product shell in The Pond with Watchtower, Dock, EVS, VACS, Site Content, and role-aware entry surfaces
Control-plane awareness and enterprise outcome modeling in the Pond
Security direction with Keeper-first secrets, Zero Trust boundary, and named offering permissions
most_critical_gaps: Duplicate ownership remains across legacy and modern systems for some outcomes
Release and repo discipline are not yet clean enough for predictable enterprise promotion
Permission and trust enforcement are strong in major lanes but not yet universal
Operational maturity still needs stronger release observability and service-level governance

domains.name: Truth and Collection
domains.scope: Canonical facts, collection orchestration, retry/closure posture, and shared read models.
strengths: Morning closure and advisory governance are now materially stronger
Most major reporting and app surfaces already depend on this truth stack
gaps: Legacy collection assumptions still exist in Portfolio_Monitoring and adjacent scripts
Service-level observability is still weaker than source-level observability
next_moves: Retire remaining accidental collection ownership outside Data_Collection
Add release and service provenance to operational monitoring

domains.name: Pond Product Shell
domains.scope: Primary operator shell, governed surfaces, role-aware navigation, and control-plane integration.
strengths: The Pond now has a coherent shell and growing system-awareness model
Role-aware UX and offering-level permissions are established
Watchtower and /system give the platform an enterprise self-model
gaps: Some surfaces still need the same depth of action-level enforcement and role tuning
Some report and dashboard outcomes still sit outside the canonical app shell
next_moves: Continue absorbing legacy dashboard/navigation outcomes into Dock and app-native views

domains.name: Security and Identity
domains.scope: Keeper secret authority, Cloudflare Zero Trust boundary, role and offering authorization, and machine identity posture.
strengths: Security architecture direction is now explicit and mostly canonical
Named offering permissions are now real in both UI and API
VACS and Site Content trust posture were materially improved
gaps: Trust evidence and enforcement are not yet uniformly complete across all lanes
Some transitional fallback and mixed-boundary assumptions still need closure
next_moves: Close remaining trust-review and transitional nodes surfaced by Watchtower
Make route-level trust evidence and permission evidence part of release readiness

domains.name: Outcome Ownership and Consolidation
domains.scope: Canonical ownership by business outcome across reports, dashboards, content ops, validation, and monitoring.
strengths: The canonical outcome map now exists and is browser-visible
Accepted specialization versus consolidate-now systems are explicitly named
gaps: Portfolio_Monitoring still overlaps Watchtower and Data Collection outcomes
Portfolio_Dashboard still overlaps Dock and analysis/navigation outcomes
The PIB / POP Brief / Spotlight family still needs one formal architecture
next_moves: Run the first consolidation wave on Portfolio_Monitoring and Portfolio_Dashboard
Publish a formal briefing-family architecture and entry model

domains.name: Release and Operational Maturity
domains.scope: Promotion, worktree discipline, branch/release separation, deployment provenance, and service-level runbooks.
strengths: There is now much better awareness of workstreams, lanes, and ownership
Control-plane visibility and trust remediation are much more mature than before
gaps: The repo remains too dirty and mixed for enterprise-grade promotion confidence
Release provenance and deployment discipline are not yet standardized enough
next_moves: Establish a clean release path and stop promoting from mixed dirty worktrees
Track deployment provenance, environment parity, and service-level incident/runbook readiness

priority_workstreams.name: Canonical Owner Consolidation
priority_workstreams.description: Remove duplicate ownership across legacy and modern systems so each major outcome has one clear canonical home.
exit_criteria: Portfolio_Monitoring no longer holds canonical operational ownership
Portfolio_Dashboard no longer acts as a parallel default navigation layer
PIB / POP Brief / Spotlight family has a published enterprise architecture

priority_workstreams.name: Release and Repo Discipline
target_outcomes: All canonical product and platform outcomes
priority_workstreams.description: Create a clean promotion model and reduce mixed-workstream release risk.
exit_criteria: Clean release branch path is defined and in use
Promotion no longer depends on giant mixed worktrees
Service changes can be traced to coherent release slices

priority_workstreams.name: Security Completion
priority_workstreams.description: Finish the remaining trust-review and transitional lanes so enterprise posture is enforced, not just described.
exit_criteria: Highest-risk Watchtower trust nodes are closed or moved to aligned posture
Named offering permissions cover the remaining major governed lanes
Release readiness includes trust and permission evidence

priority_workstreams.name: Service Observability and Runbook Maturity
priority_workstreams.description: Elevate observability from collection/source health into service and release health.
exit_criteria: Watchtower can show service-level release and runtime posture
Deployment provenance and environment drift are visible
Canonical runbooks are tied to owned services and outcomes

next_90_days.focus: Ownership, release hygiene, and top trust closures
moves: Finalize canonical owner enforcement for overlapping outcomes
Stand up clean release path and promotion rules
Use Watchtower to close the highest-value trust-review nodes
Migrate Portfolio_Monitoring outcome ownership into Data Collection + Watchtower
Migrate Portfolio_Dashboard outcome ownership into Dock + app surfaces
Complete action-level permission coverage on remaining major offerings
Formalize briefing-family architecture and user entry model
Add service-level observability and deployment provenance
Normalize release, security, and runbook discipline across canonical owners
